label: Beaches
blurb: The world's most-ranked beaches, from Lonely Planet to Condé Nast.

places.name: Grace Bay
places.why: Three miles of powder-fine sand over a shallow turquoise shelf, calm enough for kids and repeatedly voted the world's top beach.

places.name: Eagle Beach
places.why: Wide white sand with the two lone fofoti trees everyone photographs; trade winds keep it cooler than the Caribbean norm.

places.name: Seven Mile Beach, Grand Cayman
places.why: A long developed strip of soft sand and calm, clear water right along the main hotel row.

places.name: Varadero Beach
places.why: A 20 km sand spit shared by resorts, still one of the most consistently turquoise stretches in the Caribbean.

places.name: Trunk Bay
places.region: Virgin Islands National Park, St John
places.why: An underwater snorkel trail rings the bay, though cruise-day crowds can overwhelm the small beach.

places.name: Playa Norte
places.why: Shallow, current-free water off a small ferry-town island makes this one of the calmest swims in the Mexican Caribbean.

places.name: Playa Paraiso
places.why: Backed by a Maya clifftop ruin, the water stays a startling turquoise even a few strokes out.

places.name: Playa Flamenco
places.why: A mile of white sand shaped like a horseshoe, kept undeveloped since the US Navy left the island.

places.name: Shoal Bay East
places.why: A reef just offshore keeps the surf gentle over sand that stays powder-white even at midday.

places.name: Pink Sands Beach
places.why: Crushed coral gives the three-mile beach a genuine pink tint, most visible at the north end near sunset.

places.name: Horseshoe Bay
places.why: Pink-tinted sand between coral outcrops, sheltered enough for swimming even when the Atlantic is up.

places.name: Seven Mile Beach, Negril
places.why: An uninterrupted arc of white sand lined with beach bars, warmer and calmer than Jamaica's north coast.

places.name: Bavaro Beach
places.why: Barrier reef keeps the surf down along this long resort coastline, one of the busiest beaches in the Caribbean.

places.name: Playa Rincon
places.why: A three-kilometre wild beach backed by coconut palms and a mountain, reachable only by boat or dirt track.

places.name: Manuel Antonio Beach
places.why: Rainforest runs down to the sand inside a national park small enough that capuchin monkeys turn up on the beach.

places.name: Red Frog Beach
places.why: A jungle boat ride gets you to this surf-exposed beach named for the tiny red poison-dart frogs in the woods behind it.

places.name: Grand Anse Beach, Grenada
places.why: Two miles of soft sand a short ride from the capital, gently shelving and rarely crowded for its size.

places.name: Anse Chastanet
places.why: Volcanic dark-and-gold sand under the Pitons, with a reef close enough to snorkel straight from shore.

places.name: Playa Blanca, Barú
places.why: The whitest sand near Cartagena, a short boat ride from the colonial city and busy with day-trippers by late morning.

places.name: Cabo San Juan
places.why: A rock outcrop splits two coves inside a jungle-and-desert national park with no road access.

places.name: Máncora Beach
places.why: Peru's warmest coastal water and a reliable left-hand point break draw surfers and beach-bar crowds alike.

places.name: Tortuga Bay
places.why: A 45-minute walk from town reaches this surf beach and, past the point, a calmer lagoon where marine iguanas bask.

places.name: Playa El Tunco
places.why: A black volcanic-sand beach around a distinctive rock islet, the hub of El Salvador's surf scene.

places.name: Playa Santa Teresa
places.why: A laid-back surf-town beach on a peninsula reached mostly by unpaved roads, known for its sunsets.

places.name: Playa Conchal
places.why: Crushed seashells instead of sand give this beach its pale, crunchy texture underfoot.

places.name: Bahía de las Águilas
places.why: A remote seven-kilometre beach inside a national park, reachable only by boat or a rough dirt track.

places.name: Orient Bay Beach
places.why: A long resort beach on the French side of a divided island, split between family and clothing-optional sections.

places.name: Big Major Cay (Pig Beach)
places.why: Swimming pigs wade out to greet boats on this uninhabited cay, now one of the most photographed beaches in the Bahamas.

places.name: Playa Kenepa Grandi
places.why: A cliff-backed cove on Curaçao's rugged west coast, calmer than the open Caribbean side of the island.

places.name: Sorobon Beach
places.why: A shallow, reef-protected lagoon makes this the Caribbean's most reliable flat-water windsurf beach.

places.name: Maracas Bay
places.why: Trinidad's most popular beach, a curved bay backed by rainforest hills and famous for its bake-and-shark stalls.

places.name: Copacabana Beach
places.why: Four kilometres of promenade and sand backed by the city itself, packed on weekends with football games and vendors.

places.name: Ipanema Beach
places.why: Framed by the Dois Irmãos peaks, split into numbered postos where different Rio social scenes each claim a stretch.

places.name: Baía do Sancho
places.why: Reached by a ladder down a cliff crack, this reef-sheltered bay admits only a limited number of visitors a day.

places.name: Praia do Rosa
places.why: A surf town beach where southern right whales calve just offshore between June and November.

places.name: Praia da Ferradura
places.why: A near-closed horseshoe bay keeps the water flat calm, a favourite for families and stand-up paddling.

places.name: Playa Brava
places.why: The open-ocean side of the peninsula, rougher and less crowded than the bay beach a few blocks over.

places.name: Cabo Polonio
places.why: No grid power and no paved road; a 4x4 truck across the dunes is the only way in, past a sea lion colony.

places.name: Bahía Inglesa
places.why: Turquoise water more Caribbean than Pacific, cooled by the Humboldt current despite the desert backdrop.

places.name: Punta Sal
places.why: Calm, warm water near the Ecuadorian border, quieter than Máncora and popular with Peruvian families.

places.name: Waikiki Beach
places.why: The most famous stretch of sand in the Pacific, backed wall-to-wall by hotels and almost always crowded.

places.name: Lanikai Beach
places.why: Powder-soft sand facing two small offshore islets, with residential streets as the only public access.

places.name: Hanalei Bay
places.why: A two-mile crescent under jagged green cliffs, calm in summer and a serious big-wave break in winter.

places.name: Wailea Beach
places.why: Calm, resort-lined sand with some of Maui's best snorkeling right off the shore at either point.

places.name: Papohaku Beach
places.why: Three miles of wide sand with almost no development and a shorebreak too rough for most swimming.

places.name: Papakolea Green Sand Beach
places.why: Olivine crystals from a collapsed cinder cone give this remote beach its distinctive green tint.

places.name: Siesta Key Beach
places.why: Quartz sand so fine it stays cool underfoot even at midday, on a wide Gulf Coast beach with a party pier nearby.

places.name: South Beach
places.why: Art Deco lifeguard towers line a wide beach that doubles as the city's most visible social scene.

places.name: Cannon Beach
places.why: Cold Pacific water and the 235-foot Haystack Rock make this one for walking and tide pools, not swimming.

places.name: Coronado Beach
places.why: Mica flecks in the sand catch the light, on a wide beach beside the historic Hotel del Coronado.

places.name: El Matador Beach
places.why: Sea-stack rocks and a steep bluff staircase make this small Malibu cove better for photos than long swims.

places.name: Ocracoke / Cape Hatteras
places.why: Undeveloped barrier-island sand backed by dunes and a wild pony herd a short ferry ride from the mainland.

places.name: Myrtle Beach
places.why: 60 miles of wide, flat sand built around boardwalks, mini-golf and family resorts on the Grand Strand.

places.name: Coast Guard Beach
places.why: Wide Atlantic sand backed by dunes, cold water even in summer, and a grey seal colony often visible offshore.

places.name: Assateague Island
places.why: A barrier-island beach where feral horses wander onto the sand, undeveloped along its whole federal stretch.

places.name: Chesterman Beach
places.why: A cold-water surf beach on temperate rainforest coast, tidal enough to walk out to Frank Island at low tide.

places.name: Cavendish Beach
places.why: Red sandstone cliffs meet fine sand on the island's north shore, warm enough to swim by regional standards in summer.

places.name: Wasaga Beach
places.why: The world's longest freshwater beach on Georgian Bay, a summer-only inland-sea swim for Toronto day-trippers.

places.name: Playa Balandra
places.why: A shallow, protected cove on the Sea of Cortés known for a wind-carved mushroom rock and near-zero waves.

places.name: Playa Zipolite
places.why: A strong shorebreak and undertow keep this bohemian beach for wading, not casual swimming.

places.name: Playa Delfines
places.why: One of the few free public beaches in Cancún's hotel strip, with a strong shorebreak and the city's photo sign.

places.name: Navagio Beach
places.why: A rusted shipwreck sits on white sand under towering limestone cliffs, reachable only by boat.

places.name: Elafonissi Beach
places.why: Crushed shell gives parts of the sand a pink tint across a shallow lagoon that wading families cross at low tide.

places.name: Balos Lagoon
places.why: A shifting sandbar splits turquoise lagoon from open sea, reached by a rough dirt road or tour boat.

places.name: Myrtos Beach
places.why: White pebble and sand drop steeply into deep blue water below a switchback cliff road that frames every photo.

places.name: Sarakiniko Beach
places.why: Wind-carved white volcanic rock looks lunar rather than tropical; there is barely any sand to speak of.

places.name: Voidokilia Beach
places.why: A near-perfect sand crescent backed by dunes and a lagoon, overlooked by a Frankish castle on the headland.

places.name: Egremni Beach
places.why: White cliffs drop 200 metres to a long sand beach rebuilt with steps after a 2015 earthquake landslide.

places.name: Porto Katsiki
places.why: White cliffs drop to a small beach reached by a steep staircase, one of the most photographed in the Ionian.

places.name: Playa de Ses Illetes
places.why: Caribbean-clear shallows over white sand, day-tripped hard from Ibiza in summer.

places.name: Cala Macarelleta
places.why: A small pine-backed cove next to its larger sibling Macarella, reached by a coastal footpath, no road access.

places.name: Cala Comte
places.why: Rock islets offshore and a west-facing shore make this the island's best-known sunset beach.

places.name: Playa de Bolonia
places.why: A wide Atlantic beach beneath Europe's tallest coastal sand dune, backed by a Roman ruin, not a hotel.

places.name: Playa de las Catedrales
places.why: Cathedral-like sea arches only show at low tide; a permit is required in summer to walk the sand.

places.name: La Concha Beach
places.why: An urban shell-shaped bay ranked among Europe's best city beaches, calm behind Isla de Santa Clara.

places.name: Praia da Marinha
places.why: Ochre limestone stacks and sea caves ring a small beach reached by a steep staircase cut into the cliff.

places.name: Praia da Falésia
places.why: Six kilometres of ochre cliffs above pale sand, one of the Algarve's longest and least crowded main beaches.

places.name: Praia do Guincho
places.why: Consistent Atlantic wind and swell make this a windsurf and kitesurf beach, not a swimming one.

places.name: Praia do Camilo
places.why: A wooden staircase drops through an ochre rock cleft to a tiny cove threaded with sea arches.

places.name: Praia da Adraga
places.why: Rock stacks and a strong Atlantic swell make this a surfers' beach below the Sintra hills, cold water year-round.

places.name: Praia de Odeceixe
places.why: A river meets the Atlantic here, so a warm lagoon sits beside cold ocean surf at the same beach.

places.name: Sperlonga Beach
places.why: A whitewashed hill town looks down on a long sandy beach split by a rock promontory with Roman grotto ruins.

places.name: Cala Goloritzé
places.why: A UNESCO-listed cove under a limestone spire, reached only by boat or a 90-minute hike down the Selvaggio Blu coast.

places.name: Cala Mariolu
places.why: Small white pebbles known locally as 'grains of rice' shelve into vivid blue water below sheer limestone walls.

places.name: Spiaggia dei Conigli
places.why: Loggerhead turtles nest on this protected beach, accessible only on foot down a cliff staircase.

places.name: Spiaggia del Principe
places.why: Pink-grey granite boulders shelter a small cove that is the Costa Smeralda's most exclusive stretch of sand.

places.name: Zlatni Rat
places.why: A pale pebble spit that shifts shape with the current, backed by pine woods and windsurf schools.

places.name: Sveti Stefan Beach
places.why: Pink pebble sand facing a fortified islet village, split between a public stretch and the resort's private side.

places.name: Durdle Door
places.why: A natural limestone arch frames a steep-shingle Jurassic Coast beach, cold-water swimming only.

places.name: Woolacombe Beach
places.why: Three miles of Atlantic-facing sand with a reliable beginner surf break and dunes behind.

places.name: Rhossili Bay
places.why: A five-kilometre sweep of sand below a clifftop path, exposed enough that a shipwreck skeleton still shows at low tide.

places.name: Luskentyre Beach
places.why: Turquoise water and white shell sand look tropical, until the Atlantic wind and cold water say otherwise.

places.name: Camber Sands
places.why: The only large dune system on England's southeast coast, wide enough at low tide to lose the crowds.

places.name: Étretat Beach
places.why: Chalk cliffs and a natural arch made this pebble beach a favourite subject of Monet and Courbet.

places.name: Plage de Palombaggia
places.why: Pink-tinted sand under umbrella pines, backed by red rock and busy with day-trippers from Porto-Vecchio in summer.

places.name: Pampelonne Beach
places.why: Five kilometres of sand lined with exclusive beach clubs, the social centre of the French Riviera summer scene.

places.name: Reynisfjara
places.why: Black basalt sand, hexagonal columns and a dangerous sneaker-wave surf make this one to watch, not swim.

places.name: Haukland Beach
places.why: White sand and turquoise water under jagged Arctic peaks, cold enough to swim in only briefly even in July.

places.name: Nida Beach
places.why: A wide Baltic beach backed by Europe's tallest shifting sand dunes on a forested spit shared with Russia's Kaliningrad.

places.name: Jūrmala Beach
places.why: A 32-kilometre Baltic sand strip and pine forest that has been Riga's seaside retreat since the 19th century.

places.name: Kaputaş Beach
places.why: A narrow gorge staircase of some 180 steps drops to a small, brilliantly turquoise cove.

places.name: Ölüdeniz Beach
places.why: A lagoon closed off by a sand spit is the landing zone for paragliders launching off Babadağ mountain above.

places.name: Patara Beach
places.why: An 18-kilometre undeveloped dune beach doubles as a loggerhead turtle nesting site behind Lycian ruins.

places.name: Blue Lagoon, Comino
places.why: A shallow sandbar between two islets colours the water an intense turquoise, mobbed by day-trip boats in summer.

places.name: Nissi Beach
places.why: A sandbar to a small islet lets you wade out into open water, backed by one of Cyprus's busiest party strips.

places.name: Camps Bay Beach
places.why: The Twelve Apostles mountains drop straight to white sand and a cold Atlantic, backed by a palm-lined promenade.

places.name: Boulders Beach
places.why: Granite boulders shelter a small beach shared with a breeding colony of African penguins.

places.name: Noordhoek Beach
places.why: A wide, wild eight-kilometre beach with a strong current that makes it better for horseback rides than swimming.

places.name: Anse Lazio
places.why: Granite boulders bookend a white-sand bay repeatedly rated one of the world's best, no road runs along it.

places.name: Anse Source d'Argent
places.why: Pink granite boulders and shallow reef-protected water make this the most photographed beach in the Seychelles.

places.name: Anse Georgette
places.why: Only reachable by boat or through a golf course, this stays quieter than its neighbour Anse Lazio.

places.name: Anse Volbert
places.why: Shallow and reef-protected, this is the most swimmable of Praslin's main beaches, lined with small guesthouses.

places.name: Belle Mare Beach
places.why: A long lagoon-protected east coast beach lined with resorts, calm enough for swimming at any tide.

places.name: Le Morne Beach
places.why: A UNESCO basalt monolith towers over a lagoon that draws kitesurfers to its protected reef pass.

places.name: Nungwi Beach
places.why: Deep water close to shore means swimming here isn't ruled by the tide the way much of Zanzibar's coast is.

places.name: Paje Beach
places.why: Wide tidal flats turn into a reliable kitesurf launch when the wind picks up over the reef.

places.name: Diani Beach
places.why: A barrier reef holds back the Indian Ocean swell along a long, white coral-sand beach south of Mombasa.

places.name: Watamu Beach
places.why: A marine national park just offshore protects coral gardens that snorkelers can reach straight from the sand.

places.name: Benguerra Island Beach
places.why: Dhow sails pass a remote archipelago beach known for giant dune systems and dugong sightings offshore.

places.name: Tofo Beach
places.why: Whale sharks and manta rays gather offshore, drawing divers to a laid-back fishing-village beach.

places.name: Anakao Beach
places.why: A Vezo fishing village beach reachable only by boat, facing a barrier reef with almost no development.

places.name: Andilana Beach
places.why: Calm, shallow water over white sand at the quiet north end of Madagascar's main resort island.

places.name: Essaouira Beach
places.why: Steady trade winds off a wide Atlantic beach have made this Morocco's windsurf and kitesurf capital.

places.name: Legzira Beach
places.why: Ochre-red sea arches once flanked this beach; one collapsed in 2016, and the surf here keeps swimming risky.

places.name: Grand Anse, Réunion
places.why: A lagoon pool cut into black volcanic rock offers safe swimming beside a beach with dangerous open-ocean currents.

places.name: Santa Monica Beach
places.why: A 24-kilometre dune-backed Atlantic beach with almost no shade and a surf too rough for casual swimming.

places.name: Kribi Beach
places.why: Fine sand beaches either side of a fishing town, with the Lobé Falls dropping straight into the sea nearby.

places.name: Tarkwa Bay Beach
places.why: A boat-only sandbar beach cut off from Lagos traffic by the harbour channel, popular for a car-free day out.

places.name: Busua Beach
places.why: A relaxed surf-town beach on the Gulf of Guinea, one of the few in West Africa with a beginner surf school.

places.name: Cap Skirring Beach
places.why: A quiet palm-lined Atlantic beach in Senegal's greener south, well off the main Dakar tourist route.

places.name: Jumeirah Beach
places.why: A groomed urban beach facing the Burj Al Arab, popular for its skyline view more than its swimming.

places.name: Bandar Khayran Beach
places.why: A fjord-like inlet beach reached only by boat, known for coral and dolphin sightings just offshore.

places.name: Ras Al Jinz Beach
places.why: Green turtles nest on this remote beach in numbers rare outside a handful of sites worldwide.

places.name: Gordon's Beach
places.why: A busy, Blue-Flag city beach that anchors Tel Aviv's promenade, popular with paddleboarders at dawn.

places.name: Ras Um Sid Beach
places.why: A coral reef drops close to shore beneath a lighthouse, one of the Red Sea's easiest shore dives from a beach.

places.name: Ramlet al-Baida
places.why: Beirut's last public sandy beach, a busy strip against a skyline of high-rises.

places.name: Umluj Beaches
places.why: Turquoise lagoons and white sand along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast have earned it the nickname 'the Maldives of Saudi'.

places.name: Radhanagar Beach
places.why: Untouched forest runs to the sand on an island reachable only by ferry from Port Blair.

places.name: Palolem Beach
places.why: A calm, palm-lined crescent bay that stays gentle enough to swim across most of the year.

places.name: Varkala Beach
places.why: Red laterite cliffs top a beach lined with cafes, one of the few places in Kerala where cliff meets sand.

places.name: Om Beach
places.why: Twin coves shaped like the Om symbol, quieter and less developed than Goa's beaches to the north.

places.name: Agatti Beach
places.why: A shallow turquoise lagoon rings this coral island beach, one of the few Lakshadweep atolls open to visitors.

places.name: Unawatuna Beach
places.why: A sheltered bay reef keeps the water calm, making this Sri Lanka's most reliable swimming beach.

places.name: Mirissa Beach
places.why: A crescent fishing-town bay that doubles as the launch point for the island's best blue whale watching.

places.name: Cox's Bazar Beach
places.why: A 120-kilometre unbroken sand beach, among the longest natural beaches anywhere, backed by a busy tourist town.

places.name: Maafushi Beach
places.why: One of the few Maldivian beaches on an inhabited local island rather than a private resort, with a bikini section marked off.

places.name: Vaadhoo Bioluminescent Beach
places.why: Bioluminescent plankton light the shallows blue on clear, moonless nights, best seen well after sunset.

places.name: Nacpan Beach
places.why: Twin four-kilometre beaches split by a headland, still mostly undeveloped despite El Nido's tourist boom.

places.name: White Beach, Boracay
places.why: Four kilometres of fine white sand along the island's main strip, closed and rehabilitated for pollution in 2018.

places.name: Alona Beach
places.why: A dive hub beach with easy reef access, busier and more developed than the rest of Panglao's coast.

places.name: Railay Beach (West)
places.why: Limestone cliffs cut this peninsula off from the road network entirely; longtail boats are the only access.

places.name: Maya Bay
places.why: Closed to overnight visitors and boat mooring for long stretches since 2018 to let the reef recover from the crowds.

places.name: Freedom Beach
places.why: A boat- or trail-only cove that stays calmer and cleaner than the developed beaches of Phuket's west coast.

places.name: Nai Harn Beach
places.why: A lagoon-like bay beside a lake, calm in the dry season and a serious surf break when the monsoon swell turns on.

places.name: Sunrise Beach, Koh Lipe
places.why: The busiest of Koh Lipe's three beaches, with a shallow reef flat that empties out at low tide.

places.name: Nai Yang Beach
places.why: A national-park beach near the airport, quieter than Phuket's tourist strip and shaded by casuarina trees.

places.name: Klong Prao Beach
places.why: Koh Chang's longest beach, backed by a lagoon and mangrove, quieter than the island's northern strip.

places.name: Kuta Beach
places.why: Bali's original surf-and-sunset beach, now a wide stretch of sand backed by dense shopping streets.

places.name: Nusa Dua Beach
places.why: A reef offshore keeps the water calm along this manicured resort-enclave beach on Bali's southern tip.

places.name: Kelingking Beach
places.why: A steep, unofficial cliff trail down a T-rex-shaped headland reaches a small beach with a dangerous current.

places.name: Pink Beach, Komodo
places.why: Red coral fragments tint the sand pink, on a beach reachable only by boat inside the national park.

places.name: Gili Trawangan Beach
places.why: No motor vehicles on the island at all; horse carts and bicycles reach a beach known for turtle snorkeling.

places.name: An Bang Beach
places.why: A laid-back fishing-village beach a short bike ride from Hoi An's old town, with a strong seasonal undertow.

places.name: My Khe Beach
places.why: A long, flat city beach that Forbes once rated among Asia's finest, now backed by a fast-growing skyline.

places.name: Sao Beach
places.why: White sand and shallow turquoise water on the quieter south of an island now connected by direct flights.

places.name: Ti Top Island Beach
places.why: A small beach at the foot of an island viewpoint, the only easy swim stop among Ha Long Bay's limestone karsts.

places.name: Tanjung Rhu Beach
places.why: A quiet north-shore beach facing a mangrove estuary, calmer and less developed than Langkawi's main Pantai Cenang.

places.name: Perhentian Kecil Beach
places.why: A backpacker-favourite island beach with easy reef snorkeling, closed to visitors during the monsoon each year.

places.name: Sipadan Beach
places.why: A tiny oceanic island beach with a strict daily diver cap, sitting atop a wall that drops 600 metres just offshore.

places.name: Ngapali Beach
places.why: A quiet fishing-coast beach with a gentle slope and few of the crowds found elsewhere in Southeast Asia.

places.name: Otres Beach
places.why: A quieter alternative to Sihanoukville's main strip, backed by low-key beach bars rather than casinos.

places.name: Koh Rong Beach
places.why: A long, undeveloped white-sand beach with bioluminescent plankton visible in the shallows after dark.

places.name: Kabira Bay
places.why: A glass-boat bay too current-prone for swimming, known instead for black pearl farms and coral viewed from the surface.

places.name: Yonaha Maehama Beach
places.why: Seven kilometres of fine white sand along a shallow, reef-protected Okinawan coast.

places.name: Emerald Beach
places.why: A man-made but reef-fringed beach beside the Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium, calm and shallow for families.

places.name: Yalong Bay
places.why: A resort-lined bay marketed as China's tropical beach answer to Hawaii, warm year-round.

places.name: Hyeopjae Beach
places.why: White coral sand faces a small volcanic islet, one of the calmest and most photographed beaches on Jeju.

places.name: Haeundae Beach
places.why: Korea's most famous city beach, packed shoulder to shoulder with sun umbrellas every summer weekend.

places.name: Baisha Bay
places.why: Fine white sand at Taiwan's southern tip, used as a filming location and busiest during the summer festival season.

places.name: Shek O Beach
places.why: A sheltered bay beach on the quiet side of Hong Kong Island, popular with surfers when a typhoon swell rolls in.

places.name: Whitehaven Beach
places.why: Silica sand so pure it stays cool underfoot, swirling into the turquoise shallows at Hill Inlet next door.

places.name: Bondi Beach
places.why: Australia's best-known city beach, a surf break, ocean pool and coastal walk within a single suburb.

places.name: Cable Beach
places.why: 22 kilometres of sand famous for camel trains at sunset, with tides among the most extreme in Australia.

places.name: Wineglass Bay
places.why: A perfect curve of white sand seen best from the ridge above, cold water even at the height of summer.

places.name: Turquoise Bay
places.why: A drift snorkel lets you float over coral just metres from shore, one of the easiest reef swims anywhere.

places.name: Hyams Beach
places.why: Long listed for having some of the whitest sand on record, though summer weekends bring parking chaos.

places.name: Cottesloe Beach
places.why: A Perth institution for a sunset swim, with a groyne-protected patch that stays calm even with an onshore wind.

places.name: Four Mile Beach
places.why: A stinger net marks a safe swimming patch during jellyfish season on this long, flat tropical beach.

places.name: Lucky Bay
places.region: Cape Le Grand National Park, WA
places.why: Kangaroos regularly lie on the sand here, on a beach whose whiteness rivals anywhere in Australia.

places.name: Palm Cove Beach
places.why: A shaded, paperbark-lined beach north of Cairns, calmer than the open coast but still under stinger nets.

places.name: Squeaky Beach
places.why: Quartz sand grains squeak underfoot, on a beach at the southernmost tip of mainland Australia.

places.name: Ninety Mile Beach
places.why: A single unbroken Tasman Sea beach long enough that a public road once ran along the sand at low tide.

places.name: Cathedral Cove
places.why: A limestone archway frames the beach, reachable only by a coastal walking track or by kayak.

places.name: Hot Water Beach
places.why: Dig a shallow pit at low tide and geothermal water seeps up hot enough to sit in beside the cold surf.

places.name: Piha Beach
places.why: Black iron-sand surf beach overlooked by Lion Rock, with a dangerous rip that claims lives most summers.

places.name: Onetangi Beach
places.why: The longest beach on a vineyard-covered island a short ferry ride from Auckland.

places.name: Matira Beach
places.why: One of the few genuinely public beaches on an island otherwise ringed by private resort motu.

places.name: Muri Beach
places.why: A shallow lagoon with four small motu islands offshore, calm enough to wade out for a long way.

places.name: Champagne Beach
places.why: Fine white sand that fizzes underfoot at the waterline gives this remote beach its name.

places.name: Natadola Beach
places.why: One of the few white-sand beaches on Fiji's main island with no fringing reef right at the shoreline, so waves break on the sand.

places.name: Waya Island Beach
places.why: A remote island-hopping chain reached only by boat, with beaches split among small backpacker resorts.

places.name: Anse Vata Beach
places.why: A city beach inside the world's second-largest lagoon, calm and shallow thanks to the barrier reef far offshore.

places.name: Long Beach, Peleliu
places.why: A sandbar in the middle of the lagoon appears only at low tide, a stop on Rock Islands boat tours.

places.name: Lalomanu Beach
places.why: A palm-backed beach with traditional open-air fales for sleeping right on the sand, rebuilt after the 2009 tsunami.

places.name: Ha'atafu Beach
places.why: The only reliable surf break beach on Tonga's main island, with a marine reserve reef just offshore.
